# Movable diagonal simplex points: exact roof penalty and one-sided depth comparison

Let \(d\ge1\), let
\[
T_d=\{X\in\mathbb R^d:X_i\ge0,\ \sum_iX_i\le1\},
\]
and give each fiber \(\{p\}\times r_pT_d\), \(p\in P\), its ordinary \(d\)-volume, where \(P\subset\mathbb R^n\) is finite and \(r_p>0\). Fix \(j\in P\), write \(\Delta_p=p-j\), and assume
\[
r_p\le r_j+b\cdot\Delta_p\qquad(p\in P)
\tag{1}
\]
for some \(b\). Every actual convex common-vertex simplex family satisfies this touching sampled majorant condition: the finite Farkas proof, including boundary bases and lower base rank, is given in **candidate 42889f299dc055c9**, Section 3.

Write \(G_j(y)=A_\mu(j,y)\) for **absolute** original mixed depth, the infimum of the masses of all closed ambient halfspaces containing \((j,y)\). The quantities below are not normalized by the total mass. Define the positive-normal restricted quantity, also for \(y\) outside the own fiber, by
\[
P_j(y)=
\inf_{\substack{a\in\mathbb R^n\\w\in\Delta_{d-1}}}
\sum_{p\in P}
\left|r_pT_d\cap\{a\cdot\Delta_p+w\cdot X\ge w\cdot y\}\right|,
\quad
\Delta_{d-1}=\{w_i\ge0,\ \sum_iw_i=1\}.
\tag{2}
\]
Then \(G_j(y)\le P_j(y)\), and \(P_j\) is coordinatewise nonincreasing and invariant under coordinate permutations.

Put \(q=r_j/(d+1)\). The conclusions are:

* On the upper diagonal segment, \(q\le t\le r_j/d\),
  \[
  G_j(t\mathbf1)=P_j(t\mathbf1),
  \tag{3}
  \]
  and this common value is nonincreasing in \(t\).
* On the lower segment \(0\le t\le q\), let \(t'=r_j-dt\). Then
  \[
  P_j(t'\mathbf1)\le G_j(t\mathbf1)\le P_j(t\mathbf1).
  \tag{4}
  \]
  If also \(t'\le r_j/d\), the left side is the actual depth
  \(G_j(t'\mathbf1)\). Thus for
  \[
  \frac{r_j(d-1)}{d^2}\le t\le \frac{r_j}{d+1},
  \qquad
  G_j(t\mathbf1)\ge G_j((r_j-dt)\mathbf1).
  \tag{5}
  \]
* A deepest point in the entire own fiber can be chosen on
  \[
  \{t\mathbf1:0<t\le q\}.
  \tag{6}
  \]
  This is a movable segment, not an own-centroid selector.
* Equation (12) below gives an exact compact finite-dimensional all-normal optimization throughout the diagonal. Its additional coefficient is tied to the positive normal; it cannot be removed or separately optimized.

These statements do not require any normalization of the integer lattice. In applications \(P\subset\mathbb Z^n\); the base coordinates and the single shared tilt are retained.

## 1. The swapped candidate and the direction of comparison

A closed containing halfspace may be translated inward until its boundary passes through the candidate. For \(y=t\mathbf1\), \(0\le t\le r_j/d\), write a through-point margin as
\[
L(p,X)=a\cdot\Delta_p+u\cdot(X-t\mathbf1).
\tag{7}
\]
For nonzero \(u\) with a negative coefficient choose
\(u_i=\min\{0,u_1,\ldots,u_d\}<0\). Exchange the zero vertex with vertex \(r_pe_i\) on every source fiber:
\[
(\sigma_{p,i}X)_i=r_p-\sum_\ell X_\ell,\qquad
(\sigma_{p,i}X)_\ell=X_\ell\quad(\ell\ne i).
\]
This is a volume-preserving affine involution of that fiber. At the candidate its image is
\[
s_i(t)=\sigma_{j,i}(t\mathbf1),\qquad
s_i(t)_i=r_j-dt,\quad s_i(t)_\ell=t\quad(\ell\ne i).
\tag{8}
\]
With \(v_i=-u_i\) and \(v_\ell=u_\ell-u_i\) for \(\ell\ne i\), we have \(v\ge0\), \(v_i>0\), and the exact identity
\[
L(p,\sigma_{p,i}X)
=a\cdot\Delta_p+v\cdot(X-s_i(t))+u_i(r_p-r_j).
\tag{9}
\]
By (1) the genuine ambient margin
\((a+u_i b)\cdot\Delta_p+v\cdot(X-s_i(t))\)
is no greater than the right side of (9). Dividing by \(\sum_\ell v_\ell>0\) gives a positive-normal cap through the swapped candidate whose mass on every fiber is at most the original cap mass.

If \(u\ge0\), the original cap itself is in the positive class through \(t\mathbf1\). If \(u=0\), for large finite \(R\) the cap
\[
R\,a\cdot\Delta_p+X_1-t\ge0
\]
retains the full fibers on strict positive base traces, excludes strict negative traces, and cuts only a subset of each whole boundary fiber originally captured. Finiteness of \(P\) gives such an \(R\). This handles the non-null boundaries of vertical caps; it does not discard them.

It follows that
\[
G_j(t\mathbf1)\ge
\min\{P_j(t\mathbf1),P_j(s_1(t)),\ldots,P_j(s_d(t))\}.
\tag{10}
\]
Coordinate permutations make all the swapped quantities equal. For \(t\ge q\), \(s_i(t)\le t\mathbf1\) coordinatewise, proving (3). For \(t\le q\), we have
\(t\mathbf1\le s_i(t)\le t'\mathbf1\), proving (4) and (5).

For clarity, averaging the swapped candidates gives
\((r_j-t)\mathbf1/d\), but the convexity of depth regions does **not** upgrade (10) to a lower bound at that average. The swap is fiberwise and generally is not an ambient source symmetry. Section 5 gives an exact failure even in dimension one.

There is a slightly larger valid same-point region: if
\(y\in r_jT_d\) and \(r_j-\sum_\ell y_\ell\le\min_i y_i\),
then every swapped candidate is coordinatewise at most \(y\), so the same proof gives \(G_j(y)=P_j(y)\).

## 2. An exact positive-normal representation with its roof term

No majorant approximation is needed to retain the full problem. For a given \(t\), define
\[
\begin{aligned}
F_0(t;a,w)&=\sum_{p\in P}
\left|r_pT_d\cap\{w\cdot X+a\cdot\Delta_p\ge t\}\right|,\\
F_i(t;a,w)&=\sum_{p\in P}
\left|r_pT_d\cap
\{w\cdot X+a\cdot\Delta_p
\ge t+w_i[r_p-(d+1)t]\}\right|,\quad 1\le i\le d.
\end{aligned}
\tag{11}
\]
The exact formula is
\[
\boxed{
G_j(t\mathbf1)=
\min_{0\le i\le d}\ \inf_{\substack{a\in\mathbb R^n\\w\in\Delta_{d-1}}}
F_i(t;a,w).
}
\tag{12}
\]
All the infima can be replaced by minima over one compact tilt set, uniformly for \(0\le t\le r_j/d\); see Section 3. Coordinate permutations imply the branches \(i=1,\ldots,d\) have the same optimized value, so just branches \(0,1\) suffice.

To verify the formula, after a negative-coefficient swap set
\(S=\sum_\ell v_\ell\), \(w=v/S\), replace \(a\) by \(a/S\), and note that \(u_i/S=-w_i\). Direct expansion gives
\[
\frac{L(p,\sigma_{p,i}X)}{S}
=a\cdot\Delta_p+w\cdot X-t-w_i[r_p-(d+1)t].
\tag{13}
\]
Thus every nonvertical cap is represented by branch 0 or one of the roof branches. Conversely, for any \(w\in\Delta_{d-1}\) and index \(i\), put
\[
u_i=-w_i,\qquad u_\ell=w_\ell-w_i\quad(\ell\ne i).
\tag{14}
\]
This continuous normal is nonzero, and the actual single cap
\(a\cdot\Delta_p+u\cdot(X-t\mathbf1)\ge0\)
has exactly the branch-\(i\) mass after the fiberwise change of variables. The case \(w_i=0\) is harmless and duplicates a nonnegative-normal case. Vertical caps cannot improve the infimum by the finite-tilt domination already proved.

The source threshold in a roof branch need not be affine in \(p\), but (13)–(14) show exactly why it still represents one original ambient cap. Its coefficient \(w_i\) belongs to the **same** positive normal \(w\); allowing an independent coefficient or independent fiber tilts would change the problem.

At \(t=q\) the roof correction is \(w_i(r_p-r_j)\). More generally, in (13) the majorant (1) supplies the affine lower margin
\[
(a-w_i b)\cdot\Delta_p+w\cdot X-t
+w_i[(d+1)t-r_j].
\]
On the upper segment its last term is nonnegative, so the cap through \(t\mathbf1\) obtained by dropping that term is a subset. On the lower segment its sign reverses. Formula (12) retains exactly this term instead of assuming the own-centroid reduction extends unchanged.

## 3. Uniform compactness of the shared tilt

Let \(L=\operatorname{span}\{\Delta_p:p\in P\}\) have dimension \(m\). Components of the tilt perpendicular to \(L\) do not matter. If \(m=0\), use \(a=0\). Otherwise choose an orthonormal map \(E:\mathbb R^m\to L\), put \(v_p=E^T\Delta_p\), and set
\[
C=\max_{p\in P}\max\{r_p,r_j\},\qquad
B=C\max_I\|V_I^{-1}\|_\infty,
\tag{15}
\]
where \(I\) ranges over the \(m\)-element sets of independent rows \(v_p^T\).

In any branch let \(\tau_p\) be the threshold appearing on the right side of (11). For branch \(i\ge1\), it is the convex combination, with coefficients \(1-w_i,w_i\), of \(t\) and \(r_p-dt\). Consequently
\[
|\tau_p|\le C,\qquad |\tau_p-r_p|\le C
\tag{16}
\]
for \(0\le t\le r_j/d\); the same bounds hold for branch 0.

Fix \(t,w\) and a tilt. Keep its exact trace \(a\cdot\Delta_p\) if it lies in
\([\tau_p-r_p,\tau_p]\); otherwise require its replacement to be at least \(\tau_p\) on full traces or at most \(\tau_p-r_p\) on empty traces. This nonempty replacement polyhedron has no line because the \(v_p\) span \(\mathbb R^m\). A vertex has \(m\) independent active rows and right sides bounded by \(C\), hence coordinate norm at most \(B\). This is the finite-trace vertex argument of the predecessor note, now with the explicit uniform bound (16).

The replacement preserves every source mass: \(0\le w\cdot X\le r_p\), so newly attained empty supporting faces have zero \(d\)-volume. Therefore \(a=Eb\), \(\|b\|_\infty\le B\), suffices in (12). The compact set is independent of \(t,w\) and the branch. It uses real coordinates in the existing base span, not a lattice transformation.

All branch objectives are jointly continuous on this compact domain. The continuous normal \(w\) never vanishes, so a boundary hyperplane has zero \(d\)-volume in each positive fiber; dominated convergence applies. This proves attainment in (12) and continuity in \(t\).

## 4. Why a lower diagonal segment contains a deepest point

For completeness, \(G_j\) is continuous on the own fiber. Normalize every nonvertical continuous normal to Euclidean length one. Moving \(y\) by \(h\) translates each fiber threshold by at most \(|h|\), independently of its base tilt. Since the finite source fibers are bounded, their \((d-1)\)-dimensional section volumes have a common finite sum bound. The resulting cap-mass functions are uniformly Lipschitz in \(y\). Vertical cap masses are constant in \(y\); their inclusion in the infimum does not affect the Lipschitz bound. Thus \(G_j\) attains its maximum on the compact own fiber.

Depth superlevel sets are convex: if a closed halfspace of mass below a level contains a convex combination of points, it contains at least one of those points. The entire source is invariant under permutations of the continuous coordinates. Hence averaging the coordinate-permutation orbit of \(y\) cannot decrease depth:
\[
G_j\!\left(\frac{\sum_i y_i}{d}\mathbf1\right)\ge G_j(y).
\tag{17}
\]
This uses actual ambient symmetries, unlike the fiberwise barycentric swaps.

If the resulting diagonal parameter exceeds \(q\), equation (3) and the monotonicity of \(P_j(t\mathbf1)\) allow it to be replaced by \(q\). At the common vertex \(0\), the cap \(X_1\le0\) has zero \(d\)-volume on every source fiber. At the own centroid, an interior ball in the own fiber gives a positive lower bound for every cap; a vertical cap contains the whole own fiber. Thus a maximizer does not have parameter zero. This proves (6).

The archived nested intervals with lengths \((2,6,10,3)\), discussed in the predecessor note, show why the segment cannot be replaced by its centroid endpoint in general.

The own-fiber payment on this segment is nevertheless exact:
\[
A_{r_jT_d}(t\mathbf1)=|T_d|(dt)^d
\qquad(0\le t\le q).
\tag{17a}
\]
For \(t>0\), the inscribed simplex \(((d+1)t)T_d\) has centroid \(t\mathbf1\). The ordinary centroid inequality gives the lower bound
\(\Gamma_d|T_d|((d+1)t)^d=|T_d|(dt)^d\).
The cap \(\sum_iX_i\le dt\) gives the reverse bound; \(t=0\) is immediate. Thus (17a) is also a lower bound for original mixed depth at that point. It pays only the own fiber and asserts no additional external-source mass.

The separate note **candidate f803303a19217c7c** shows that taking a normal-independent minimum over every simplex-vertex comparison orbit cannot improve the own-centroid depth floor. Formula (12) retains the normal and distinguished-coordinate coupling, so it is not that independent orbit minimum.

## 5. A fiberwise swap can strictly reduce depth

Consider the actual concave interval profile with fibers
\([0,1],[0,5],[0,1]\) at bases \(-1,0,1\). The total mass is \(7\). This is the familiar three-interval family from the earlier depth and vertical-flow notes; here it calibrates the precise direction of the new comparison.

At \((0,c)\), a through-point upward cap can be written
\(X+a z\ge c\). For \(1\le c\le4\), its own contribution is \(5-c\), and its two other contributions sum to
\[
\operatorname{clip}(1-c-a,0,1)+
\operatorname{clip}(1-c+a,0,1).
\tag{18}
\]
This sum lies between zero and one: both summands cannot be positive when \(c\ge1\). It attains zero at \(a=0\) and one for sufficiently large \(|a|\). The opposite nonvertical cap has complementary mass because its boundaries have zero fiber length. Closed vertical caps contain the middle fiber and at least one endpoint fiber, hence have mass at least \(6\). It follows exactly that
\[
G_0(c)=\min\{5-c,1+c\}\qquad(1\le c\le4).
\tag{19}
\]
In particular,
\[
G_0(2)=3,\qquad G_0(3)=2.
\tag{20}
\]
The fiberwise swap takes \(c=2\) to \(5-2=3\). In dimension one this is also the averaged swapped candidate. Thus no reverse inequality or swap-depth invariance follows from the involutions. Equation (5) gives the correct direction.

## 6. An exact two-slope specialization, with the tilts still linked

Suppose \(n=1\), \(j\) is the roof breakpoint, and
\[
r_p=r_j+s_-(p-j)\quad(p\le j),\qquad
r_p=r_j+s_+(p-j)\quad(p\ge j),\qquad s_-\ge s_+.
\]
In roof branch \(i\), put \(\omega=w_i\). Then the threshold correction in (11) is equivalent to a common threshold
\[
t+\omega[r_j-(d+1)t]
\]
and the respective effective left and right tilts
\[
a_- =a-\omega s_-,\qquad a_+=a-\omega s_+,
\qquad a_+-a_-=\omega(s_--s_+)\ge0.
\tag{21}
\]
This is an exact scalar reformulation of one ambient cap, not two freely chosen tail cuts. Neither \(\omega\) nor the effective tilts may be independently optimized. The unequal-positive-normal counterexample in **candidate 15438eaf9a458a13** also remains applicable to the unpenalized branch.

The standard-library verifier **../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_movable_diagonal_simplex_roof_penalty.py** checks the exact algebra, the inverse normal, all sign regions, the uniform threshold bounds, and the interval calibration. The general proof is the argument above; it does not depend on a numerical screen or a conjectural OC selector.
